correctness.rationale: An explicit exposed-face argument identifies the one-run adjacency criterion without relying on degeneracy assumptions. Direct tensor-product diagonalization proves the all-profile integer spectral list and matrix-tree product; an exact transition-bound lower/upper proof identifies binary distances, while third-symbol interpolation and a nonadjacent witness establish the sharp ternary diameter. Independent LP/breadth-first/dense spectral/exact determinant checks passed for their specified finite domains. The analytical proof handles arbitrary positive layer cardinalities \(\ge2\) and all \(k\ge1\).

originality.rationale: Full relevant sections of Blanchard–De Loera–Louveaux (arXiv:2001.09575) and Borgwardt–De Loera–Finhold (arXiv:1603.00325) were inspected; the 2020 work attributes adjacency to Rispoli, and the binary metric matches the classical halved cube, both expressly disclaimed as novelties. None of the inspected primary results states or implies the full mixed-layer spectral/tree product and alphabet-sensitive graph-distance classification without new specialization and proof. The inaccessible 1992 full text and unindexed equivalent descriptions remain explicit risks; search nonmatches are not treated as proof of uniqueness.
residual_risks: The entire Rispoli 1992 original article was inaccessible; an exact stronger statement there cannot be excluded, though the cited secondary source gives the relevant adjacency lemma.
A classical isomorphic graph family other than the explicitly credited binary halved cube might already encode the q-ary spectrum and all-pairs metric.
Computational checks are finite; no independent third-party validation has been performed.

value.rationale: The findings determine the complete one-skeleton metric in two infinite uniform subfamilies and the full Laplacian spectrum/spanning-tree complexity for arbitrary complete layered networks. The diameter switches from unbounded \(\lceil k/2\rceil\) in binary layers to exactly two in every uniformly \(q\ge3\) network, exposing a sharp geometric path-pivot complexity threshold not quantified by general Hirsch bounds. The objects and invariants are standard and naturally motivated, not arbitrary finite slices.
